title: Legacy search sort values must be mapped, not string-replaced, to index field names
answers: search results are in random/arbitrary order
sort dropdown (recently viewed, alphabetical, errors) doesn't sort results
why does my saved sort option no longer sort dashboards
legacy sort value from old search UI is ignored by unified search
body:
Symptom: Search results appear in arbitrary order with sort direction lost, specifically for sort options carried over from the old search UI ("viewed-recently-desc", "errors-recently-asc", "alpha-desc", etc.), which persist in browser storage and the page URL.
Root cause: public/app/features/search/service/unified.ts derived the API sort field with naive string replacement (`sort.replace('_sort','').replace('name','title')`) that only handled the new UI's own `name_sort` value; other legacy values passed through unchanged and matched no index field.
Fix pattern: replaced the string replacement with an explicit `Record<string,string>` lookup table (`uiSortValues` in public/app/features/search/service/unified.ts) mapping every known sort value (current and legacy) to the real index field name, with a `-` prefix for descending; unmapped values fall through unchanged via `toSortParam`.
Constraints: applies when translating user-facing/stored values (sort, filter, column names) into backend/index identifiers where the set of legacy values is enumerable; use string transforms only when the mapping is truly mechanical, not when multiple unrelated old UIs feed different vocabularies into the same field.
